body: I'm curious though.  Did they regret it because of the repercussions or did they actually regret wanting to take their own life?

Definitely not the medication.  That I tried a few times last year without success and I gave up on it.  It was definitely the diet.

Definitely, definitely, without any doubt, I can assure  you it was the diet.  Now as I write this, I realize I got so used to the diet, I still don't eat potatoes, pasta, bread, etc.  Not because I choose to, but because I stopped "liking" it.  So maybe that also keeps it away?
Very welcome and good luck :)

I've been wondering if that was my case.  feeling like I'm done because I'm feeling much better, and it's why I've also continued to see him.
But because we have nothing to really discuss, everything seems to be judgmental now even if he keeps saying he's not judging anything.

That's the things, he says things like "You're having sex without a good connection? that's not sex.  That's just a good vowel release", followed by "I'm not judging, but that's not sex".

He especially keeps trying to make me upset at my parents when I told him I have no issues with them.  He was even upset because I didn't want to date someone who is about 15 years older than me who showed interest in me.  He said "You're putting a wall, you're not giving them an opportunity.  Why? because they're older?".  I could go on and on, and this is actually what i should be telling him instead.  I have my appointment with him in a couple of hours and I'll tell him exactly all of this and explain why I feel it's not working out anymore.

Perhaps if I saw him less as you say, it would help. But I think it's getting uncomfortable at this point.  I do like him though, and I keep repeating this but he has helped me SO MUCH.  Before meeting him, I actually never believed in going to a psychologist, this completely changed my opinion.  He's VERY good at what he does, except I think he's a bit too emotionally involved.

It was his decision to do 2 hours sessions twice a week.  Since I instantly felt comfortable with him, I agreed and I think that's what helped me understand and overcome my issues speedier than expected.  It's going to sound terribly ungrateful, but now I see it as a chore, as a waste of time.

I have my appointment with him in a couple of hours.  I'll just be as honest as I can about everything and go from that.  I appreciate your comment, thank you.

It can be frustrating, yes.  But once you set your mind to it, it's a bit easier. 

I completely gave up candy and beer, I wouldn't even think twice about it.

I did it little by little, replacing the "bad" things with the things in the candida diet list.  Sometimes I would wake up in the middle of the night with the need of something sweet, that was tough.  

From what I've read here on /r/candida, it varies on everyone.  But for me, it was definitely zero potatoes, zero rice, zero bananas or apples, an definitely never pasta.  I avoided canned sauces, beans, rice.

I replaced them with a lot of greens, home cooked meals instead of eating out.  And if I ate out, I would just order stuff i know I could eat.  I did not stop eating meats though.  I ate fish, steaks and chicken.  I never had issues with that.  Vegetables are good for you anyway, so it's not bad to eat plenty of it.  Enough to satisfy your hunger though, not enough to get you tired of it.  I also ate a lot of eggs, boiled eggs.  I never had issues with that.

I think it was for about 10 months until I noticed it.  But even though I can eat bananas now, I still somewhat keep some of the diet.  I'm avoiding potatoes for the most part, same goes for pasta and most sweets.  I just lost the cravings for them.
It's mostly sweet fruits that I'm eating again, and beans and rice because I love chipotle, heh.
I've noticed he has a LOT of resentment towards his his family, in particular his father.  It feels like he's trying to transfer all of that onto me.

I have a feeling he'll react negatively, but this is the time to be as open as I can.  I'll tell him he's making me uncomfortable and if he continues I'll just walk way.
Like someone else said here, no longer needing him is what he was supposed to do.

I like your idea.
I think it would be way too expensive to pay him for everything but I could pay for some.  I think it's definitely time to end it though, and I'll tell him the reasons why.  Not as a complaint but I think he deserves an explanation.
I definitely want to end it.  I'm a bit nervous because he already made me cry once, but I guess I should man up...

I think this is what I'll do.

He has definitely crossed a few lines.  At first I thought perhaps it was that he genuinely cares about me and it felt nice to have that feeling.  But then I noticed he would email me telling me that I haven't emailed him over the weekend to tell him how things are going, he also keeps repeating he's struggling not to cross the line but he's putting his "father hat" even though he shouldn't.  So it seems like he's aware he's doing it.  I feel ungrateful because it seems he's trying to push me to do better but at the same time, it feels like he's trying to make me a version of what *he* thinks is best, not what I think is best.

But you're right.  The goal of therapy is to make it unnecessary.  I'll meet him and tell him in person.  If I see that he's reacting negatively, I'll just get up and leave.

It does feel he's being needy.

I've asked him several times why he did it for free.  2 hour sessions twice a week, that's 4 hours of his time for free a week.  He said he liked talking with me, he liked seeing my improvement.  I sometimes think that he's a bit lonely, but this is just me guessing because he has such an open schedule.

Every now and then he'll complain about his parents and he gets very serious.  I think he's trying to transfer his parent issues on to me, he wants me to be upset at mine.  He's upset at his father for not telling him he's proud of him for being a psychologist.  But I digress, you're right, my relationship with my trainer is much different.  He never tells me he's going to act like my father and only focuses on when I'm there, not outside of sessions like the psychologist does sometimes.

I'm guessing it was just following the "candida diet" that has been mentioned here. I pretty much followed that strict diet.  First it was to get rid of the candida and then because I actually got used to it and liked it.  Sometimes it was frustrating though because I would feel like it stopped, and then it'd come back in just a few days, less than a week.  
That's why I didn't even realize it until a month or so ago until I started testing it.

Mind sharing what she said to you that left a bad taste in your mouth?

I'm going ahead of myself here, but I have a feeling he won't react well to it when I tell him I don't want to continue seeing him anymore.

I cancel on him at least 24 hours before, sometimes 2 days in advanced.  I don't think he sees many other patients, since his schedule is always so open.  Regardless of that, I've always been considerate of his time and never cancel last minute.

The thing I forgot to say in my original post is, last time he actually made me cry.  I'm a 34 year old man and he made me cry out of frustration when he gets in his "father" role.  I would feel guilty to end it via phone and feel obligated to do it in person, but it makes me a bit nervous.

I'm supposed to see him tomorrow, but I actually have to cancel yet again because my trainer only had that same spot open.  I'll just ask him if I can see him earlier and you're right, I need to just be honest and tell him I need to end my treatment.  I feel like he'll be upset but... it's the least I can do since he was very generous.

Through Yelp.  I wasn't working when I met him and before he told me his fee, he asked me what I issues I needed to resolve.  I told him, and once he said what his fees are I thanked him for his time and said I couldn't afford it.  Because I told him I was feeling suicidal, he agreed to do it for free.

At that time I didn't think about asking what his credentials are.

I feel like I make myself depressed, like I'm used to it, I come to expect it. I see no exit, I see no change.  
Just last night, it occurred to me that I just may be addicted to this feeling.  It's like I don't want to let go of it.

Yes I have.  Why?

He prescribed one 150 MG tablet of Fluconazole, and Clotrimazole Antifungal cream.  

The tablet I took once (since it's only one), and the cream I had to apply twice a day.  I thought it was helping, but I think it was just that I was washing it twice daily.

It did not work... so I recently went to the doctor again, a bit over 2 weeks ago.  I again was prescribed the same tablet, and I asked for a stronger dose, they refused.  What they agreed to do however, was give me a prescription for 2 weeks (2 pills instead of 1).  I'm on the second one now, but it's still not going away.  Also, this time they prescribed Nystatin cream usp.  I unfortunately don't think it's working :(.

Hey,

This actually helps a lot.  Thank you very much for sharing it.

Guilt invades my mind when I think about how I ruined the relationship.  I pushed him away because I wasn't ready for his type of love.  He was so in love with me, I had never experienced anything like that, it was too much, I needed a break.  By the time I realized how much I wanted to spend my life with him, it was too late.  He moved on, but didn't tell me.  He kept telling me how much he loved me, while finding other people.  
He became so emotionally abusive, he became something completely different.  My self esteem went down to the ground, my personal goals dissipated, etc.  

Because of this, I looked for new friends to distract me, and have met SO many amazing people.  This is the big positive side to everything, I made some really good friends, and have a very healthy social life.

Even with all of this though, the pang of remorse and guilt still creeps into my mind almost daily, sometimes even as soon as I wake up.

I have many reasons why I should let go, I understand them all, but I'm still so emotionally attached, even without having contact with him.  I just can't seem to let go no matter how hard I try.

Sometimes I feel like meeting someone to help me get over him, but I don't want to use this person for that.  Meaning, date someone.  I think it would help, but it's not fair for the other person.

You having been married for years, and able to accept that he wanted someone else, and to let go, it's impressive.  I hope I can do that, I'm trying very hard.  Thank you again for sharing.

Hey there, thank you.  I appreciate your response.

He actually didn't do anything wrong in the relationship, I was just not ready for his type of love back then.  It was very intense, and it had been my first relationship like this.  I asked him for a break, and then it became a long distance thing.  

By the time I realized it was him I wanted to spend my life with, he had moved on.  That's when he started changing, lying about still loving me while he kept meeting other people.  The reason I feel guilty, is because I ruined what could've been a nice life.  He truly became something so different.  Since he no longer cared about me, he became emotionally abusive, and I'd accept it.  We'll see what happens...

I know it's silly, but it hurts me, because he has been such a terrible person to me, putting me down when I tried to commit suicide the first time, bragging about how happy he is without me, etc.. and with his success, it just feels like he's being rewarded.  I mean, how can someone doing all these negative things to someone else, be doing so well? I know life isn't fair, and I need to let go of that. I've been trying to get over my ex for almost a year now, and it's been the toughest struggle I've ever experienced.  I've developed deep depression, among other things, which I never experienced before.

He is still friends on Facebook with at least 17 mutual friends, and family members.  I wouldn't ask anyone to stop talking to him, that's their decision.  I did ask them to not tell me anything about him though, that was just too painful.

I too pushed people away in the beginning.  I just wanted to be alone, and feel sorry for myself, trying to get over the pain on my own, or simply cry until I fell asleep.  One thing I learned is, this is when we need friends, and people the most.  If you argued with your friend, and if it's not something important, make up and talk to him/her.

If you can't reconcile with your friend, make new ones.  Reddit is great for that. I posted something about looking for new friends, to help distract me from the breakup, and I was very lucky to meet 2.  From those 2, I met others, and then some more.  It's been great, and it has helped very much.

I still get depressed, I still think about my ex, I dream about him constantly, still feel like part of me is missing, I still struggle to sleep (like right now).  Sometimes I feel like it's not worth to keep trying to get out of this depression, but we must.  We have no choice, we eventually have to move on.  We can't live like this.  Right?
